liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
liebermann.notes: Roger Twysden's edition in Wheloc's Archaionomia (1644) used for Hn, CHn cor and Hn Lond a text of the Lond class, Co and Or–Gi family. What Schmid prints as Tw for Wl art retr comes not from Wheloc but from Wilkins, who admits mixing Wl art and Wl art retr, so perhaps no separate manuscript lies behind it.

entries.text_de: Roger Twysden benutzt in seiner Ausgabe für Wheloc’s Archaionomia (1644) von Hn, u. S 547, mit CHn cor und Hn Lond, u. S. 521. 524, einen Text der Classe Lond und zwar der Familie Co und Or-Gi8. [Was Schmid9 zu Wl art retr, u. S. 489 als Tw druckt, stammt nicht aus Whelock, sondern aus Wilkins Leges Anglosax., der p. 217a gesteht, Wl art und Wl art retr vermengt zu haben, also vielleicht keine besondere Hs. benutzt.]
entries.text_en: Roger Twysden, in his edition for Wheloc’s Archaionomia (1644) of Hn, below, p. 547, with CHn cor and Hn Lond, below, pp. 521. 524, uses a text of the class Lond, and specifically of the family Co and Or-Gi8. [What Schmid9 prints as Tw for Wl art retr, below, p. 489, comes not from Whelock but from Wilkins Leges Anglosax., who admits on p. 217a that he mixed up Wl art and Wl art retr, and so perhaps used no particular MS.]

transcription.doubts: 'u. S 547' printed without period after S. Second 'Wl art' and 'Wl art retr' near the end are roman, not bold. 217<sup>a</sup> is a note letter. Wheloc / Whelock both spellings as printed.
